newsitem.title: FRANCE: French TV show suspended after Chirac murder spoof.
newsitem.headline: French TV show suspended after Chirac murder spoof.

text.p: A French television channel said on Tuesday it was suspending a popular satirical programme which ran a spoof news report that President Jacques Chirac had been murdered.
Canal Plus said it was suspending "Le Vrai Journal" (The True News) after France's broadcasting watchdog complained about a weekend sketch parodying the U.S. film "Pulp Fiction".

In the show, Chirac, Prime Minister Alain Juppe and Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre are murdered by professional killers representing French people angered by their leadership of France over the past year and half.

A statement said network executives had decided to modify the format and make changes to the staff of the programme. "For these needs, the broadcast will be suspended for four weeks from November 3," it said.

During a meeting earlier on Tuesday, the Higher Audiovisual Council (CSA) watchdog reminded Canal Plus to respect rules according to which "the company is prohibited from broadcasting programmes, whose content go against the law and public order".
The CSA summoned Canal Plus chairman Pierre Lescure for an explanation.
